Stephanie - thanks for the quick review last week. Our legal and security teams reviewed the DPA and pushed back on the deletion timeline language. Two asks that are blockers for us: 1) a requirement for 'individual on-demand erasure' to complete across primary and backups within 7 calendar days and 2) delivery of a 'signed certified erasure manifest' confirming deletion from all systems (including backup snapshots).

We understand operational constraints, but given our regulated customers we need contractual assurances. Can Redwood commit to 7 days end-to-end and to a manifest delivered to our security team? If not, please propose the firmest timeline you can guarantee and explain the technical or legal exceptions (e.g., lawful hold).

Attaching our redline (Aether_DPA_redlines_v4.pdf) and a short list of acceptance criteria.

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for the annotated redline. We absolutely take erasure and proof seriously. A few initial points so we're explicit up front:

- We differentiate between logical deletion (removal from live tenant indexes) and deletion from immutable backup snapshots. Backups are typically retained for recovery and compliance, and purging them is operationally more complex.
- We do provide a certified erasure manifest today for on-prem/private customers as an optional deliverable; for hosted customers we can generate a signed manifest but the timeline varies depending on the retention/backup window.

Counter-proposal (operational + contractual language we believe is supportable):
1) Individual erasure (logical removal from live datasets and search indexes): within 48 hours of request (subject to normal authentication/verification steps).
2) Backup snapshot purge: Redwood will schedule purge from backups within 30 days and complete physical removal within the subsequent snapshot cycle (worst-case 60 days total).
3) Certified erasure manifest: delivered within 10 business days after the final removal event, signed by an authorized Redwood security representative and including a manifest of scopes (primary, replicas, backup snapshots, region).
4) Exceptions: lawful holds, active litigation, or customer-configured archived snapshots will pause the purge and will be explicitly called out in the manifest.

Technical rationale: forcing guaranteed 7-calendar-day physical purge from all backups would require us to change snapshot cadence or to implement accelerated backup rehydration+purge workflows (possible, but non-trivial and would impact cost / availability). We can offer a program-level commitment for customers with reserved capacity / Private deployments to tighten those windows.

I'm looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (infra) to align legal wording and confirm the infra constraints. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the fields in the manifest that matter most to your audit team.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Security Programs

Elena / team — appreciate the specificity. From a contractual drafting perspective we propose the following redline language that mirrors Stephanie's operational proposal but gives Aether stronger auditability: 

"Redwood will execute individual erasure requests as follows: logical removal from active customer datasets within forty-eight (48) hours of validated request; deletion from backups and immutable snapshots within thirty (30) days after Redwood's next scheduled backup window, with physical removal completed no later than sixty (60) days after the request. Redwood will provide a certified erasure manifest, signed by an authorized Redwood representative, within ten (10) business days following confirmed removal from all applicable systems. Exceptions due to lawful hold or customer-initiated archive settings will be documented in the manifest."

Notes on proof: the manifest will include timestamped identifiers, snapshot IDs, region, and the scope (primary, replica, snapshot). It will not include low-level storage block-level hashes by default; if Aether requires hashed proof we can include an addendum that scopes additional proof and cost.

If that language looks acceptable to Aether we can fold it into the DPA and proceed. If you remain firm on 7 calendar days for backups, please confirm whether that is a hard contractual requirement or a negotiable target for high-sensitivity customers.

Best,

Quick infra note to clarify the "why" on the 30-60 day window and to offer mitigations we can operate: 

1) Snapshot cadence: our hosted service takes incremental snapshots every 24 hours and a full snapshot weekly for regionally replicated tenants. Purging a specific user's records requires identifying all snapshot deltas that contain pointers to those objects and either regenerating snapshots without the data or marking tombstones and expiring them on the next compaction cycle.
2) Recovery SLAs: accelerating snapshot compaction to guarantee <7 day physical purge across all customers would require dedicating a per-account expedited purge pipeline. That introduces compute and IO costs and could impact recovery point objectives for other tenants.

Operational mitigations we can offer Aether as part of AETH-4821: 
- For dedicated customers (Redwood Dedicated or Private) we can configure a shorter retention cycle (e.g., 7-14 day backup purge window) as part of the deployment.
- As an add-on for hosted customers: expedited purge credits that trigger an accelerated compaction job and commit to a 14-day physical purge (instead of 60) for a defined fee.
- BYOK note: when customers use BYOK with customer-managed keys, we can render snapshots inaccessible by rotating keys on the relevant snapshot blobs; that provides a cryptographic effective deletion step that may satisfy auditors, but it's distinguishable from physical block deletion and must be described in the DPA.

Happy to provide a short appendix with estimated costs and timelines for the expedited purge option if Aether wants contractual 7-day (or 14-day) guarantees.

—Karthik

Proposed contractual pickup for Section X (Erasure):
- Logical removal from active datasets: 48 hours after validated request.
- Backup snapshot purge: Redwood will remove the subject data from backup snapshots within thirty (30) days after Redwood's next scheduled backup window and complete physical removal no later than sixty (60) days after request.
- Expedited option: For customers on a dedicated plan or those who purchase an expedited-purge add-on, Redwood will commit to purge from backups within fourteen (14) calendar days after request. Expedited option will be priced and described in Appendix G.

If Aether requires cryptographic proof (e.g., block hashes or key rotation evidence), that will be treated as a scoped addendum with potential costs.
- Exceptions: lawful holds, court orders, or customer-initiated archives will be documented; Redwood will not be in breach where deletion is restricted by such holds.
